title: Blueberry Oath
logline: At the market stone Boof swears the only oath a wish allows: to spend it when the want is true — and learns the shadow price, that every spent wish owes a coincidence to a stranger.
epigraph: Every wish is paid twice: once by the wisher, once by someone who never hears about it.
description: Chapter 7 of Lore.Land: Blueberry Oath. An oath is a key given in public, paid in fruit, with the unspent wish as witness. Boof swears to spend the wish only when the want is true, while the Fool samples the sworn-oath trope and the shadow names the correction someone else will pay.

content.text: The great market stone stood at the center of the square, its granite top worn smooth and dished by centuries of pressing palms. Boof had come to do the one thing the council could not do for her and BaneWAP could not undo: bind herself, in public, to the wish. For an oath here was understood exactly as the Genie had taught her to understand keys — it was a

children.text: , handed to the whole watching town at once, so that no one hand could ever secretly grow it. The public half was the words. The private half was paid in fruit, pressed into the rock where centuries of sworn juice had gone before. And the witness was the egg itself, set warm upon the lip of the stone: an unspent wish, watching a promise being made about its own spending.

content.text: Boof pressed a blueberry into the stone. Skin split; juice slipped into the groove worn by other paws and palms. She would spend the wish when the want was true. Not for spite, not for show. Not because a crowd was waiting. The square fell quiet enough to hear a stall-cloth flap. Beneath her other paw, the egg grew warmer.

content.text: But every oath sworn in noon light casts one. The shadow lay across the grooves, dog-shaped, egg-shaped, cold, and it was not BaneWAP's — it was the oath's own dark half, the clause nobody reads aloud. The Genie read it anyway, because pricing things was the one habit he had not liquidated. "Understand what you have promised to spend," he said quietly. "A wish redirects momentum. Redirected momentum lands somewhere. Every spent wish — mine, yours, anyone's — owes one coincidence to a stranger. A cart delayed, a letter misdelivered, a rain moved to a different field. Someone always pays the correction, and they are never at the ceremony."

content.text: The sworn oath — oldest trope on the shelf. Kings swear on swords. She swore on fruit. Returned with interest.

From the awning he laid it out like a set: the hero's vow, sampled from every saga that ever rattled a mead-hall — swords kissed, blood mingled, thrones promised. He honked it back changed: no blade, no blood, one blueberry, one working dog, and a clause the sagas always skipped — the stranger's bill. That was the interest. An oath that admits its shadow is worth ten that don't.

sections.figcaption: The oath-stone: public words, private fruit, one warm witness — and the clause in shadow.

content.text: After the crowd thinned, Boof stayed, chin against the granite. Purple juice dried beside older stains. Somewhere, a stranger would be late because she had wished: a cart missed, a letter lost, rain on the wrong field. She could neither find them nor warn them. The oath gave her no way around that. She sat until the stone cooled beneath her chin. Around her, the square returned to its smaller business. A merchant shook rain from an awning, a child chased a rolling spool, and two neighbors resumed an argument they had set aside for the ceremony. None of them knew which stranger would catch the turn of her wish. Perhaps that stranger was having an ordinary afternoon too, expecting a letter, counting the hours to supper. Boof watched the spool lodge between two stones. The child knelt to free it. She stayed a little longer, until the crowd had become people again.

She pressed one last blueberry into the central groove until the purple juice welled up and filled the old gold-veined cracks. Payment that smelled true. The lattice-edged shadow at the alley mouth withdrew without a sound — an oath witnessed in public is a poor thing to bid on. Boof lifted the egg back into her sling and turned her nose south, toward the ancient well that keeps every face without stealing a single soul.

content.text: Swear small, pay in fruit, and tip the stranger you will never meet.
His voice thinned with the market bell. Stalls folded, shadows lengthened, and far away a cart kept someone waiting. No one in the square heard its driver call.

loreItems.description: An oath is a key given in public and paid in fruit, with the egg — the unspent wish — as witness to a promise about its own spending.
Boof's oath: never spend the wish for spite, show, or hurry — only when the want is true and finally sayable.
The shadow price: every spent wish owes one coincidence to a stranger. Someone always pays the correction, and they are never at the ceremony.
The Fool samples the sworn-oath trope — swords and blood in every saga — and returns it with interest: one blueberry, one dog, and the clause the sagas skip.
